about:
# ForeverRings

![ForeverRings logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alde/ForeverRings/master/assets/logo.png)

Radial action rings for World of Warcraft: Forever. Hold a key, a ring
of icons opens around the cursor, point at one and let go to use it.
Rings fill themselves from your bags and spellbook, so a new potion or
a new rank of a buff turns up without you touching anything.

Inspired by [OPie](https://www.townlong-yak.com/addons/opie) and
AutoBar. It shares no code with either and is not affiliated with
their authors.

## Installing

Copy this folder into the Forever client's AddOns folder, keeping the
name `ForeverRings`:

```
World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/ForeverRings
```

The TOC targets interface `16001`.

## Using it

1. Type `/frings` to open the options window.
2. Pick a ring, click the **Key** button and press the key you want.
3. In game, hold that key, aim at a slice and release.

Releasing near the centre of the ring cancels. Hovering a slice shows
its tooltip, and cooldowns show as a swipe with the seconds left.

Rings work in combat. Their *contents* only change out of combat: if
you use up an item mid-fight its slice greys out, and the ring catches
up when combat ends.

`/rl` reloads the UI, unless another addon has already claimed it.

## Rings

A fresh install comes with these unbound rings:

| Ring        | Holds                                                             |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Consumables | Healing potion, mana potion, other potions, elixirs & flasks, food, drink, bandage |
| Travel      | Hearthstone, teleports, portals                                   |
| Buffs       | Class buffs, conjured food and water included                     |
| Quest       | Quest items you can use                                           |
| Mounts      | Random favourite mount, then each favourite                       |
| Totems      | Your four most used totems, plus a slice opening each element ring |
| Earth, Fire, Water and Air Totems | Every totem of that element you know  |

A ring is an ordered list of slots. Each slot is either:

- a **category**, which fills itself, or
- a **fixed** spell, item or macro, dragged in from the spellbook, bags
  or macro window, or
- **another ring**, shown as a round slice with a gold rim. Moving onto
  it while holding the key opens that ring around the cursor in place
  of this one; aim and release as usual. Nesting goes one level deep,
  and a ring can't open itself.

A ring shows its first 12 actions in slot order. Change the order with
the Up and Down buttons in the options window.

### Categories

| Category           | Slices        | Picks                                         |
|--------------------|---------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Healing Potion     | one, best     | Potions that cast "Healing Potion"            |
| Mana Potion        | one, best     | Potions that cast "Restore Mana"              |
| Other Potions      | one per item  | Every other potion                            |
| Elixirs & Flasks   | one per item  | Elixirs and flasks                            |
| Food               | one, best     | Food & drink items that don't cast "Drink"    |
| Drink              | one, best     | Items that cast "Drink"                       |
| Bandage            | one, best     | Bandages                                      |
| Usable Quest Items | one per item  | Quest items with a use effect                 |
| Hearthstone        | one           | The Hearthstone, or the Hearths macro (below) |
| Teleports          | one per spell | Mage teleports, Moonglade, Astral Recall, Death Gate |
| Portals            | one per spell | Mage portals                                  |
| Class Buffs        | one per spell | Buffs, armours, aspects, blessings, weapon enchants, conjuring |
| Earth/Fire/Water/Air Totems | one per spell | Shaman totems of that element |
| Most Used Totems   | up to four    | The totems this character casts most          |
| Random Favourite Mount | one       | The mount journal's random favourite          |
| Favourite Mounts   | one per mount | Collected favourites, by name                 |

If the [Hearths](https://github.com/alde/hearths) addon is loaded, the
Hearthstone slot uses its `HEARTHS_BTN` macro instead, so the ring
rotates hearthstones along with it.

Most Used Totems counts every totem cast by this character, from the
ring or anywhere else, and keeps the counts between sessions. It is
empty until you have cast a totem, and its order catches up after
combat.

Mounts come from the mount journal. A mount you can't use where you
are still shows, rather than the ring emptying every time you go
indoors.

"Best" means highest item level, then newest item. Items above your
level are skipped. Spells cast by name, so you always get the highest
rank you know.

Items are sorted by item class, subclass and the name of the spell
they cast on use. There are no hand-kept item lists to go stale. The
spell categories do use lists of spell IDs, in
[`SpellLists.lua`](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/blob/master/SpellLists.lua). They are classic-era IDs and not
all have been checked in game, so if a spell you know is missing, its
ID is the first suspect.

## Options

`/frings` and the AddOns compartment button open a movable window. The
same controls appear under **Options → AddOns → ForeverRings**, but the
Settings panel takes over the keyboard and blocks bags and the
spellbook, so drag-and-drop only works in the window. The Settings page
has a button to open it.

The window covers:

- **Spawn animation**: none, fade in, grow, unfold from centre or
  spiral out, at 0.05–0.5 seconds.
- **Rings**: create, delete and pick a ring to edit.
- **Key**: click, then press a key with any modifiers. Right-click
  clears it.
- **Contents**: add a category, drop in a spell, item or macro, and
  reorder or remove slots.

## How it works

Each ring is a protected frame plus a hidden secure action button that
the key binding clicks. Key down shows the ring at the cursor; key up
works out which slice the cursor points at and sets the button's
action to it before the click goes through. Both steps run in the
game's restricted environment, which is what lets rings work in combat.

That slice choice is written twice: once in the restricted snippet in
[`Ring.lua`](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/blob/master/Ring.lua), and once in
[`Layout.lua`](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/blob/master/Layout.lua) for the hover highlight, because restricted
code cannot call ordinary addon functions. A test runs both all the way
round the ring to keep them in agreement.

| File              | Does                                                      |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `SpellLists.lua`  | Spell IDs for the spell categories                        |
| `Categories.lua`  | Category definitions                                      |
| `Actions.lua`     | Turns a ring's slots into slices (pure)                   |
| `Layout.lua`      | Slice directions and hit-testing (pure)                   |
| `Animation.lua`   | Spawn animation poses (pure)                              |
| `Context.lua`     | Reads bags, spells, macros and mounts for `Actions.lua`   |
| `Cooldowns.lua`   | Puts item, spell and macro cooldowns on a slice           |
| `Config.lua`      | Saved settings, migrations and every change to them       |
| `Ring.lua`        | The ring frames, secure snippet, tooltip and animation    |
| `Core.lua`        | Events, ring registry and the out-of-combat queue         |
| `Commands.lua`    | `/frings` and `/rl`                                       |
| `Options.lua`     | The options window and Settings page                      |

Saved settings live in `ForeverRingsDB` and are upgraded through
numbered migrations in `Config.lua`, so an upgrade never brings back a
default ring you deleted.

## Releasing

`## Version` in the TOC is a plain number. It started at the commit
count and goes up by one every time something lands on `master`,
whether a direct commit or a merged pull request, because each of
those is a release candidate. A pull request carries its own bump.

To release, tag a commit on `master` with its version and push the tag.

The tag starts the GitHub Actions workflow, which packages the addon
with the [BigWigs packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager).
`.pkgmeta` leaves `tests/` and `assets/` out of the download.

## Tests

The pure modules, the secure snippet, the settings migrations and the
cooldown routing are tested outside the game with LuaJIT:

```bash
luajit tests/run.lua
```

Anything that needs real frames (the panel layout, key capture, combat
behaviour) still has to be checked in game.

## Licence

MIT. See [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/blob/master/LICENSE).

# ForeverRings

## [13](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/tree/13) (2026-11-07)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/compare/11...13) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/releases)

- feat: add totem rings with most used totems  
    Adds Earth, Fire, Water and Air Totems categories, and preset rings  
    for each, opened from a Totems ring that also holds the four totems  
    this character casts most. A level 60 shaman knows about twenty  
    totems, more than one twelve-slice ring holds, which is why the  
    elements sit one ring down.  
    Most Used Totems is fed by counting UNIT\_SPELLCAST\_SUCCEEDED for the  
    player's totem casts, from the ring or anywhere else. Counts are kept  
    per character in the new ForeverRingsCharDB, by spell name so every  
    rank adds to one tally. Spell IDs can be secret values in combat on  
    this client; such casts go uncounted rather than erroring. A count  
    change requests a rebuild, so the order updates after combat. Ties  
    keep list order, and the category is empty until a totem is cast.  
    Settings migrate to schema 5, adding the five rings unless the names  
    are taken. The preset names contain spaces, so ring names may now  
    contain inner spaces; the rule against them dated from the removed  
    slash commands.  
    Totem spell IDs are rank 1 classic IDs and not yet checked in game.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat: add nested rings  
    A ring slot can now be another ring. Its slice shows the target ring's  
    first icon; moving onto it while holding the key opens the target ring  
    around the cursor in place of this one, and releasing uses whichever  
    ring is on screen. Releasing on the slice without opening it does  
    nothing.  
    Opening has to happen in restricted code to work in combat, which can  
    react to the cursor entering a protected frame but cannot run every  
    frame. Each ring slice therefore gets an invisible protected hover  
    target, 1.5 times the icon size, whose wrapped OnEnter opens the  
    sub-ring. The visible icons stay insecure so the spawn animation  
    still runs in combat. The parent header holds a frame ref per ring  
    slice, which the click snippet also uses to find an open sub-ring on  
    key up and to close one left open on key down.  
    Nesting stops at one level: a sub-ring's own ring slots are ignored,  
    and a ring cannot open itself. That resolution moves into  
    Actions.SubringAction so it is unit tested. The options window's add  
    dropdown lists the other rings under "Open another ring".  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ForeverRings

## [11](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/tree/11) (2026-11-07)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/compare/9...11) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/releases)

- docs: bump the version for everything landing on master  
    The release notes said the TOC version equals the commit count and  
    goes up with every commit. The rule is that anything landing on master  
    bumps it by one, whether a direct commit or a merged pull request,  
    because each is a release candidate. A merged pull request can add  
    several commits but only one bump, so the version stops tracking the  
    commit count; it only started there.  
    A pull request carries its own bump. This commit lands directly on  
    master, so it sets the version to 11.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- fix: add shaman weapon enchants to class buffs  
    Rockbiter Weapon never appeared in the Buffs ring because the shaman  
    weapon enchants were missing from the class buff list. Adds Rockbiter,  
    Flametongue, Frostbrand and Windfury Weapon, and fills other self-buff  
    gaps found while checking: Fear Ward, Omen of Clarity, Righteous Fury  
    and Aspect of the Beast. All are rank 1 IDs cast by name, so the  
    highest known rank is used.  
    Every commit now bumps the TOC version to the commit count, so this  
    one sets it to 10, and the README's release notes say so instead of  
    describing a bump only at release time.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# ForeverRings

## [9](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/tree/9) (2026-11-06)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/compare/0.2.1...9) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/alde/ForeverRings/releases)

- build: package releases the way Hearths does  
    Mirrors the Hearths release setup:  
    - ## Version in the TOC is a plain number. It starts at 9, the commit  
      count at this commit, and goes up by one per release from here, each  
      bump committed as "chore: bump version to N" and tagged N.  
    - Pushing a tag runs the same GitHub Actions workflow as Hearths,  
      which packages the addon with the BigWigs packager.  
    - .pkgmeta packages as ForeverRings and leaves tests/ and assets/ out  
      of the download.  
    - The TOC gains an author name, a category and an icon, and shorter  
      notes, in line with Hearths.  
    - MIT licence and a fuller .gitignore, as in Hearths.  
    The packager has no documented handling for interface 16001, so the  
    first tagged release will show whether it labels the build correctly.  
    Uploading to CurseForge also needs an X-Curse-Project-ID in the TOC  
    and a CF\_API\_KEY secret, neither of which exists yet.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat: use the Hearths macro for the hearthstone slot  
    When the Hearths addon is loaded and its per-character HEARTHS\_BTN  
    macro exists, the Hearthstone category uses that macro instead of the  
    hearthstone item, so the Travel ring rotates hearthstones along with  
    Hearths. The addon check guards against a stale macro left behind  
    after Hearths is removed; with no macro yet, the item is used.  
    Categories can now name a preferred macro this way through a  
    preferMacro field, resolved in Actions before the category's own  
    matching.  
    A macro slice would otherwise show "HEARTHS\_BTN" as its tooltip, so  
    macro slices now show the tooltip of the spell or item the macro  
    would use. Working that out moves from Cooldowns into  
    Context.MacroTarget, which the tooltip and cooldown swipe both use.  
    Hearths only targets the retail client today, so this takes effect  
    once it ships a Forever TOC.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat: add mount categories and a Mounts ring  
    Mounts come from the mount journal, which /dump C\_MountJournal ~= nil  
    confirms the Forever client has. Two categories:  
    - Random Favourite Mount casts the journal's "Summon Random Favorite  
      Mount" spell (150544) by ID, since it is not in the spellbook. With  
      no favourites set the game picks from every usable mount.  
    - Favourite Mounts gives one slice per collected favourite this  
      character can ride, sorted by name.  
    Mount usability is deliberately ignored: it flips with every doorway  
    and would empty the ring indoors.  
    Categories gain a third kind next to bag-item matching and spell  
    lists: a collect function that asks the context for its actions.  
    Rings rebuild on NEW\_MOUNT\_ADDED, and on C\_MountJournal.SetIsFavorite  
    through a hook, as favouriting fires no event of its own.  
    Settings migrate to schema 4, which adds an unbound Mounts ring unless  
    the user already has a ring with that name.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
